title: Laredo's 12th Annual Catrina Festival Takes Over La Sanbe Tonight
excerpt: Laredo honors Día de los Muertos tonight with the 12th Annual Catrina Festival — a 10-block Memorial Walk down San Bernardo ending at the Pan American…
content:
Laredo honors Día de los Muertos tonight with the 12th Annual Catrina Festival — a 10-block Memorial Walk down San Bernardo ending at the Pan American Courts, with mariachi, folklórico, altars and a best-dressed Catrín and Catrina contest, according to Tragaluz.

The Memorial Walk convenes at Vega's Interiores, 4002 San Bernardo, and the processional begins at 6:00 p.m. on Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, according to Tragaluz. The 10-block processional ends at the Pan American Courts Arts Complex.

The walk is led by Mariachi Mezcal de Tejas and dancers of the Gabriela Mendoza García Folklórico, according to Tragaluz. Participants are encouraged to carry a photograph of a deceased loved one, a recuerdo, or a small altar; organizers suggest bringing copies of photos rather than originals, and altars may be pulled on wagons. The walk concludes with placing photographs and mementos at a communal altar.

The folklórico will perform dances from the Huastecan tradition of Xantolo, described as a celebratory dance of ancestral offerings and communal renewal, according to Tragaluz.

Contests, food and art

Events include a contest for the best-dressed Catrín and Catrina, plus a crown-making workshop hosted by Laredo artist María Hinojosa, with a small fee and all materials provided, according to Tragaluz.

Food and treats come from Frontera Beer Garden vendors Katsumi, Laredo Lemonade Co., Gorilla Smoke & Grill, and El Puesto, according to Tragaluz. The monthly Chula Market vintage pop-up will run during the festival, and there is an open call for creatives to exhibit Día de los Muertos artwork.

Walk participants are urged to register in advance by calling (956) 645-2512. The Pan Am Arts Complex director is Sandra Rocha Taylor, and festival information is on Instagram @panamericancrts, according to Tragaluz.

This is Laredo's own 12th annual festival at the Pan American Courts — separate from Nuevo Laredo's Catrina festival and from the City of Laredo's Día de los Muertos celebration at North Central Park, which is also taking place today.
